name: [WEEKLY] AI/LLM Framework Web Service Spawns Shell or Network Tool (Agent-Framework Unauthenticated RCE)
description: Detects a web-facing AI/LLM framework runtime (python/uvicorn/gunicorn/node, or a framework-launched Chromium/headless browser) spawning an OS shell, recon binary, or network/download utility — the universal post-exploitation step that every unauthenticated/pre-auth RCE in this fortnight's advisories converges on. It matters now because a cluster of critical AI-tooling RCEs dropped in the last 14 days: Langflow Shareable-Playground and BaseFileComponent RCEs (CVE-2026-48519, CVE-2026-55447), Crawl4AI's AST sandbox escape, path-traversal, and Chromium extra_args injection (CVE-2026-53753 + two GHSAs), PraisonAI's Jobs-API approval bypass, Vitest Browser-Mode CDP abuse (CVE-2026-53633), Microsoft's AutoJack AutoGen Studio MCP chain, and Unit 42's Vertex AI pickle hijack — all chaining T1190 → in-process command execution. The chain spans exploit (public-facing app) and install/execution (interpreter spawns shell). It fires when an LLM-framework parent process forks a shell, recon command (whoami/id/uname), or egress tool (curl/wget/nc/socat); it will NOT fire on the framework simply serving HTTP, importing libraries, or running its own python child workers, keeping it tied to genuine command-execution behaviour rather than normal service activity. Because the framework process is never expected to spawn an interactive shell or netcat, this is alert-grade despite the breadth of covered products.
